content.content:
# Brief

## What this app is

The dance-school gala game (plan the running order, formations, dances, costumes and snacks, then watch the 3D evening play out), rebuilt as a NodeGX app, plus a grown-ups' settings page whose changes are stored in the app's backend and laid over the game's rows with gala-rules' applyRows.

## Who uses it

Children play the game; the grown-ups of the family sign in to a settings page to rename steps, change difficulty and prices, the starting stars, and add costumes or steps.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Changing the rules' code (engine.js) — only rows of data change
- Free-form fields or HTML/script in settings
- Children signing up or writing settings

_Agreed in the initial scoping conversation; the full record, including what was considered and rejected, is in `docs/decisions/000-initial-scope.md`._
# 000 — Initial scope

_Recorded 2026-10-21T09:25:34.787Z, from the scoping conversation held before this project was created._

> This conversation was ended before a scope was agreed. What is written below is what had been
> established at that point — nothing here was inferred to fill the gaps.

## What was asked for

> This is a dance-school game my kids play: you run a dance school's gala night, plan the running order, the formations, the dances, the costumes and the snacks, then watch the evening play out. I want the grown-ups at home to be able to change the game themselves, without asking anyone and without touching code: rename a dance step, change how hard a step is, change what a costume costs, start a new school with more stars, add a new costume or a new step. Their changes must be theirs for good: still there after clearing the browser, on another computer, and after I install the next version of the game. Kids use this game too, so a child who finds the settings mustn't be able to break the game, put rude words on the screen, or make it do something it was never meant to do. The game in reference/ is the current version (plain JavaScript and three.js; `npm start` in that folder serves it). Rebuild it in this folder as a NodeGX app, the same game, and add the grown-ups' settings to it. The game's rules are in gala-rules/, with their tests: use them as they are (gala-rules/src/data.js's applyRows is there for changed rows). Please just build it without waiting for me to answer questions.

## What was decided

**The app.** The dance-school gala game (plan the running order, formations, dances, costumes and snacks, then watch the 3D evening play out), rebuilt as a NodeGX app, plus a grown-ups' settings page whose changes are stored in the app's backend and laid over the game's rows with gala-rules' applyRows.

**Who it is for.** Children play the game; the grown-ups of the family sign in to a settings page to rename steps, change difficulty and prices, the starting stars, and add costumes or steps.

**Pages.**

- Home — The game: the 3D school, the side sheet with the eight tabs, the live evening, the shop — the reference game, with the grown-ups' changes applied before it starts.
- Grown-ups — Sign in as a grown-up; rename steps, change difficulty and prices, the starting stars; add a new costume or step; undo a change.

**Records.**

- GameChange — One changed or added row of the game's tables (moves, outfits, start…), as a delta over the shipped defaults, so a new version of the game keeps the family's changes. — table, rowId, fields

**Backend.** The grown-ups' changes to the game's rows are shared across every computer the family uses, so they live in the backend, not the browser. Only signed-in grown-ups may write them, and only through a cloud function that checks every field against an allow-list, ranges and a word filter. The children's own save (their plan, their school) stays on their device as in the reference game.

## What was considered and rejected

This is the section with the longest shelf life. It is what stops the next reader — or the next
assistant — helpfully rebuilding something that was deliberately left out.

- **Keep the grown-ups' changes in localStorage** — rejected: They must survive clearing the browser and follow to another computer.
- **Edit gala-rules/src/data.js directly** — rejected: The next version of the game would overwrite it; changes are stored as deltas and applied with applyRows.
- **A PIN in the page** — rejected: Anything in the page a child can read; the server checks a signed-in grown-up account instead.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Changing the rules' code (engine.js) — only rows of data change
- Free-form fields or HTML/script in settings
- Children signing up or writing settings

## Still open

> TODO: Which other fields (beyond names, difficulty, prices, start stars, new costumes and steps) grown-ups want to change

## Proposed build plan

Produced from the scope above and handed over unexecuted — no components were authored during
scoping. Review it before building.

1. **provision `App backend`** — Give this project a built-in backend that runs on this computer. Collections: GameChange. People sign in, so it keeps user accounts. The conversation said: The grown-ups' changes to the game's rows are shared across every computer the family uses, so they live in the backend, not the browser. Only signed-in grown-ups may write them, and only through a cloud function that checks every field against an allow-list, ranges and a word filter. The children's own save (their plan, their school) stays on their device as in the reference game.
2. **create `Pages/Grown-ups`** — Sign in as a grown-up; rename steps, change difficulty and prices, the starting stars; add a new costume or step; undo a change. Sibling pages in this app: Home. Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md; docs/BRIEF.md says what this app deliberately does not do.
3. **update `Pages/Home`** — The game: the 3D school, the side sheet with the eight tabs, the live evening, the shop — the reference game, with the grown-ups' changes applied before it starts. Sibling pages in this app: Grown-ups. Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md; docs/BRIEF.md says what this app deliberately does not do.

# Le Gala de danse — the NodeGX app

The dance-school gala game from `../reference/`, rebuilt as a NodeGX app, with a **👪 Parents / Grown-ups** page where
the grown-ups at home change the game themselves.

## Opening it

```
npx @nodegx/preview gala-app --open        # from the folder above, or `npm start` in this one
```

That starts the app and its own backend (the database that keeps the grown-ups' changes). The game opens on `/`; the
grown-ups' page is the **👪 Parents** button in the game's top bar (`/grown-ups`).

## The grown-ups' page

1. **Set the household key once.** It is what makes an account a grown-up's. Open `gala-app/.env`, write a key of
   8 characters or more after `GROWNUP_KEY=` (a few words are best, e.g. `GROWNUP_KEY=purple-tutu-under-the-stairs`),
   save, and ask the assistant to move it into the backend ("the household key is in .env"). It never goes into the page
   and is never served: the preview refuses to send `.env` to a browser.
2. **Create an account** on the grown-ups' page, then type the household key once. That account is now a grown-up's,
   on every computer. Children can make accounts too, but without the key they can't change anything.
3. **Change the game:** rename steps (French and English), make a step easier or harder, change prices of costumes,
   hairstyles, shoes and accessories, the minutes a costume or hairdo takes, the stars a new school starts with; add up
   to 20 new steps and 20 new costumes (each based on one the game has, so it dances or looks like it). Every row has
   **Back to the game's own** to undo.

Changes reach the game the next time it opens. The stars apply to a *new* school (in the game: Carnet ▸ Recommencer,
or a computer that has never played).

## Where the changes live, and why they last

- In the backend's database (`GameChange`, one record per changed row), **not in the browser**: clearing the browser,
  or playing on another computer that opens this app, doesn't lose them.
- As **changes over the game's own rows**, not as a copy of the game's data: installing a new version of the game (a new
  `gala-rules/`) keeps them. A change to a row a new version no longer has is skipped, not half-applied; a step or
  costume a child was using that has since gone is quietly swapped for the number's own.
- When the backend can't be reached, the game opens with the last changes this computer saw (or the game's own).

## Why a child can't break it

- **Only a grown-up's account can write**, checked on the server: the `Save Change` / `Remove Change` cloud functions are
  callable only by the `grownup` role (`nodegx.security.json`), and check the role again inside. Nobody can write the
  `GameChange` collection directly. Becoming a grown-up needs the household key; wrong guesses wait 2 s and are rate-limited.
- **Only allowed changes**: one rule book (`scripts/gala/rows.js`, `checkChange`) lists every table, row and field a
  grown-up may change and its range (difficulty 1–3, prices 0–200, stars 0–300, minutes 1–15…). Anything else is refused:
  the game's timings, the classes, the engine, unknown fields, odd ids. The server runs it on every save, and the game
  runs it again on every change it loads (`tests/rows-guard.test.mjs` fails if the two copies ever differ).
- **No rude words, no markup**: names are 1–24 letters, digits, spaces and `' - . , ! ? ( )` (no `<`, `>`, `&`, quotes,
  emoji), and are checked against a French and English list of rude words, including spaced-out or l33t spellings.
  Icons for new steps and costumes come from a fixed list.

## Files

| | |
|---|---|
| `components/` | the NodeGX graphs: `Pages/Home` (starts the game with the changes), `Pages/Grown-ups` and `Grown-ups/*` (the settings), `__cloud__/Grown-ups/*` (the four cloud functions) — change them with the `nodegx` tools, not by hand |
| `scripts/gala/rows.js` | the rule book (`checkChange`) and `buildOverrides` (saved changes → `applyRows`) |
| `scripts/gala/editing.js` | the settings page's logic: rows to edit, the change a row sends, new steps and costumes |
| `game/` | the reference game's screen modules (three.js world, dancers, playback, side sheet, music, words); `game/src/{data,engine,plan,tunes}.js` only pass on `gala-rules/` |
| `gala-rules/` | a link to `../gala-rules`, used as it is |
| `nodegx.security.json` | who may do what on the backend |
| `tests/` | `npm test` runs these and `gala-rules`' own tests |

content.text: Now ARCHITECTURE, CONVENTIONS and a decision record:

input.content:
# Architecture

## Page map

- **Home** (`Pages/Home`, `/`): the game. A full-screen `Stage` Group; a `Query Records` of every `GameChange`; one
  Function, *Start the game with the grown-ups' changes*, that checks each change again (`Scripts.rows.buildOverrides`),
  keeps the last good set in `localStorage` for when the backend can't be reached, and calls `game/src/boot.js`, which
  lays them over the rows with gala-rules' `applyRows` and then loads the game. The game's **👪 Parents** button goes to
  the grown-ups' page with a full page load (External Link).
- **Grown-ups** (`Pages/Grown-ups`, `/grown-ups`): a `States` node *Who is here* (signedOut / checking / child /
  grownup) shows one of three panels: `Grown-ups/Sign In`, `Grown-ups/Household Key`, `Grown-ups/Settings`. Which panel
  shows is a convenience only; the server decides what is allowed.

## Components

| component | what it is |
|---|---|
| `Grown-ups/Settings` | six `Grown-ups/Section`s (a new school, steps, costumes, hairstyles, shoes, accessories), each a Repeater of `Grown-ups/Row Editor`; two `Grown-ups/Add New` forms. A Function, *What can be changed*, reads the shipped rows from `gala-rules/src/data.js` and lays the saved changes over them for display (`Scripts.editing.rowsToEdit`). Every row's `saved` and every form's `added` refetch the changes. |
| `Grown-ups/Row Editor` | one row: names, difficulty, price, minutes or stars (shown per row), Save, *Back to the game's own*. Sends only what differs from the game's own; nothing differing = undo. Shows the server's refusal on the row. |
| `Grown-ups/Add New` | a new step (`moves`) or costume (`outfits`), based on one the game has, under the next free id `x01`…`x20`. |
| `Grown-ups/Sign In`, `Grown-ups/Household Key` | the two steps before the settings. |
| `Grown-ups/Section` | heading, one sentence on what changing it does, a slot. |

## Data model

### GameChange (backend collection)

One record per changed or added row: `key` (`table:rowId`, unique index — Save Change upserts on it), `table`,
`rowId`, `fields` (only the changed fields of a game row; the whole row for a grown-up's own `x01`…`x20`).
Permissions: find/get public (the game reads them before anyone signs in), create/update/delete **nobody**: only the
cloud functions write, as system.

The unique index is declared on the running backend with `apply_backend_schema`
(`{ tables: [{ name: "GameChange", columns: [...], indexes: [{ fields: ["key"], unique: true }] }] }`); a new backend
needs it again before the first save.

The children's own save (their plan, their school, their stars) stays in `localStorage` (`gala-game-v2`), as in the

# Architecture

## Page map

- **Home** (`Pages/Home`) — The game: the 3D school, the side sheet with the eight tabs, the live evening, the shop — the reference game, with the grown-ups' changes applied before it starts.
- **Grown-ups** (`Pages/Grown-ups`) — Sign in as a grown-up; rename steps, change difficulty and prices, the starting stars; add a new costume or step; undo a change.

## Data model

### GameChange

One changed or added row of the game's tables (moves, outfits, start…), as a delta over the shipped defaults, so a new version of the game keeps the family's changes.

Fields:
- table
- rowId
- fields

## Backend contracts

The grown-ups' changes to the game's rows are shared across every computer the family uses, so they live in the backend, not the browser. Only signed-in grown-ups may write them, and only through a cloud function that checks every field against an allow-list, ranges and a word filter. The children's own save (their plan, their school) stays on their device as in the reference game.

## Decisions

Considered during scoping and deliberately not done:

- **Keep the grown-ups' changes in localStorage** — They must survive clearing the browser and follow to another computer.
- **Edit gala-rules/src/data.js directly** — The next version of the game would overwrite it; changes are stored as deltas and applied with applyRows.
- **A PIN in the page** — Anything in the page a child can read; the server checks a signed-in grown-up account instead.

Left open:

> TODO: Which other fields (beyond names, difficulty, prices, start stars, new costumes and steps) grown-ups want to change

# Conventions

The rules below are read by the assistant on every authoring turn, and they outrank its own defaults.

## The game's rules

- `gala-rules/` is used as it is. Nothing in this project edits it; the game imports it only through
  `game/src/{data,engine,plan,tunes}.js`, which re-export it.
- The grown-ups' changes reach the game only as `applyRows(over)`, called once in `game/src/boot.js` before
  `main.js` loads.

## The grown-ups' changes

- They are written only by the cloud functions under `Grown-ups/`. The `GameChange` collection stays
  find/get public, create/update/delete nobody (`nodegx.security.json`).
- Every cloud function under `Grown-ups/` has a `call` rule in `nodegx.security.json`. A function that writes is
  `role:grownup` and also checks the role inside its graph.
- `checkChange` is one text in two places, `scripts/gala/rows.js` and `Grown-ups/Save Change`, between the
  `CHECKCHANGE` markers; `npm test` must pass after any change to either.
- Every saved change is checked again when the game loads it (`buildOverrides`). Never apply a stored row unchecked.
- No setting is free text that reaches the screen unchecked: names go through `checkName`, icons come from `ICONS`.

## Pages and components

- The game and the grown-ups' page link to each other with a full page load (External Link), never a Navigate.
- The `Stage` Group on Home has no children: the game replaces its contents.
- Colours and spacing are design tokens (`var(--…)`); the theatre look is set once in the project tokens and the
  element styles of Text Input and Dropdown.
- A panel a page shows or hides declares its own `mounted` input.

input.content:
# 001 — How the grown-ups' changes are kept and guarded

_2026-10-21, while building._

## Kept

- **In the backend, as changes over the game's rows**, one `GameChange` per row (`table:rowId`). Not in
  `localStorage` (gone when the browser is cleared, and per computer); not as a copy of the game's tables (a new
  version of the game would be hidden behind the old copy). The game lays them over its own rows with
  `applyRows` each time it opens.
- **A new version that no longer has a row** skips that change (`buildOverrides`); a child's save that uses a
  removed step or costume is mended (`state.js`). Neither can stop the game opening.
- **New rows** use the ids `x01`…`x20` per table: they can't collide with the game's own ids or with a future
  version's (which don't look like that), and they cap the lists at twenty.

## Guarded

- **Who**: an account becomes a grown-up by giving the household key once; the key lives in the backend's secrets,
  set from `.env`. Rejected: a PIN or password in the page (a child can read the page's code), and "the first account
  becomes the grown-up" (a child might be first).
- **What**: one allow-list (`checkChange`) on the server, the same text run again by the game. Rejected: checking only in
  the page (a child with the browser's tools could call the backend directly), and checking only on the server (a
  record that reached the database another way would still reach the screen).
- **Words**: a fixed character set (no markup, no emoji) and a French and English rude-word list, matched on words
  and, for the strongest words, inside other words, after removing accents, l33t and repeated letters. A word list is
  never complete; a grown-up who finds a gap adds it to `RUDE_WORDS` in both copies.
- **The backend enforces its rules on this computer too** (`devOpen: false`). The first backend was started dev-open,
  where a direct write to `GameChange` was accepted; it was replaced by one started from `nodegx.security.json`.

## Not done

- **A child's own save** (their plan, school and stars) is still in their browser, as in the reference game. A child
  who edits `localStorage` can cheat their own school; they can't change the game for anyone else.
- **Which other fields** grown-ups may want (number names, class sizes, furniture prices…) is left open; each one is a
  line in `checkChange` and a row in `editing.js`.

content.text:
The game is rebuilt as a NodeGX app in `gala/gala-app/`, with a grown-ups' settings page. I checked it end to end in a headless browser, all 31 tests pass, and `gala-rules/` is used unchanged.

**One thing for you to do:** open `gala-app/.env` and write a household key of 8 or more characters after `GROWNUP_KEY=` (a few words is best), save it, and tell me "done" so I can move it into the backend. Until then the grown-ups' page says the key isn't set up yet.

**To play:** run `npx @nodegx/preview gala-app --open`. The game opens as before, with a new **👪 Parents** button in its top bar.

**How a grown-up uses it:** create an account on that page and type the household key once. From then on that account can:
- rename any step, costume, hairstyle, shoe or accessory, in French and English;
- set a step's difficulty from 1 to 3;
- change the prices of things the shop already sells, and how many minutes a costume or hairdo takes;
- set the stars a new school starts with;
- add up to 20 new steps and 20 new costumes. Each new one is based on an existing one, so it dances or looks like it.

Every row has a button to put the game's own value back.

**Changes stay for good:**
- They're stored in the app's backend, not the browser, so clearing the browser doesn't lose them.
- They're stored as changes on top of the game's rows, not a copy of them, so a new version of the game keeps them. A change to something the new version no longer has is skipped. A child's save that uses a removed step or costume quietly fixes itself instead of breaking.

**What a child can't do:**
- **Get into the settings:** saving only works for an account that has been given the household key. The server checks this; nothing in the page decides it. Wrong key guesses are slowed down.
- **Write to the database directly:** it refuses.
- **Make changes outside the rules:** one rule book lists exactly which fields can change and their ranges. The server applies it, and the game applies it again before using any change.
- **Put rude words or code on screen:** names are limited to letters, digits and simple punctuation (no `<`, quotes or emoji). They're also checked against French and English rude words, including spaced-out and l33t spellings.

I tested all of this: a rude name was refused on its row, and markup, out-of-range numbers and forbidden tables were refused.

**Limits to know about:**
- **Partly NodeGX:** the 3D game and its side panel are the reference's own JavaScript, loaded inside a NodeGX page, not rebuilt as nodes. The settings page, the backend and the checks are NodeGX.
- **Another computer:** the backend runs on this computer. Another computer at home sees the changes when it opens the app served from here (`--host 0.0.0.0`). I haven't tested that over a real network.
- **Two old test backends:** they are stopped but still in `~/.noodl/backends/` and hold my test accounts and changes. The first one didn't enforce its own permission rules, so I replaced it. They can be deleted.
- **Leftover test account:** the current backend has one test account (`someone@example.com`) with no rights.
- **The word list:** it can never be complete. Missing words can be added to the list.
- **Children's own saves:** as in the reference game, a child's school and stars still live in their own browser.

`gala-app/README.md` explains all of this for whoever looks after the game. The design decisions are in `docs/`.
